1. Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes — adjust downward for the first 5–7 days.

2. Model underestimates prices during sustained upward trends — increase forecast slightly when recent history shows >78.50 and rising.

3. Model exhibits lagged response to true price spikes — forecast often peaks 1–3 days after actual spike; delay correction by 1–2 days for future forecasts.

4. Model shows mean reversion bias — overcorrects after sharp drops, leading to premature recovery; reduce forecast slope after sharp declines.

5. Model tends to overreact to short-term volatility — forecast spikes too high after minor price movements; cap forecast at +5% above recent 7-day average unless confirmed trend reversal.

6. Model underestimates long-term upward momentum — when true outcome exceeds 80.00 for 3+ consecutive days, increase forecast by 1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.

7. Model fails to capture “late-cycle” price corrections — often underestimates final 5–7 days of a 30-day forecast; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to end of forecast if true outcome shows sustained upward trend.
